headline.text: The FDA adalimumab label identifies greater infection risk with concomitant immunosuppressants, including the corticosteroid class containing budesonide.

reported.text: The warning covers corticosteroids as a class and does not quantify a budesonide-specific effect.

claims.text: The FDA adalimumab label says patients taking concomitant immunosuppressants such as corticosteroids may be at greater risk of infection; this class includes budesonide.
claims.quote: Patients 65 years of age and older, patients with co-morbid conditions and/or patients taking concomitant immunosuppressants (such as corticosteroids or methotrexate), may be at greater risk of infection.
claims.judgeRationale: The adalimumab label says patients on concomitant immunosuppressants such as corticosteroids may be at greater infection risk; budesonide is a corticosteroid and the claim keeps the 'may'.

sources.title: Appropriateness of therapy for active Crohn's disease: Results of a multidisciplinary international expert panel-EPACT II.
sources.citation: 1876-4479 3 4 2009 Dec Journal of Crohn's & colitis J Crohns Colitis

pharmacistQuestions.text: The label describes this interaction, but there seem to be no human studies of it. How is it usually handled for someone like me?
Do any of my other medicines contain Adalimumab or Budesonide, or work the same way?
Does my dose, or the time between taking Adalimumab and Budesonide, change how much this matters?
